newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 16.0/17.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 16.0/17.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 16.0/17.0 percent on Monday morning, dealers said.
They said short-term liquidity was seen tightening although Bank Indonesia supplied 339 billion rupiah into the market.
Dealers said operators were also cautious because of the approaching month-end factor.
One local bank dealer said, however, there was still some chances for arbitrage between the swap and the money market.
Overnight swap was at 0.2/0.3 and tom/next at 0.25/0.35.

"We notice the central bank is gradually draining excess rupiah from the market and raising short-term rates at the same time," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding this was to reduce speculative dollar buying.
Dealers said the absence of central bank purchase of short-term securities (SBPUs) also added to constarints in the liquidity of banks.
They said one-week and one month money were edging up because the central bank did not provide longer-term money which forced operators to borrow from the interbank market.
One- and two-week money were both at 15.50/15.75 and one- and three-month money were at 15.75/16.00 percent.
Bank Indonesia kept its interest rates for bilateral papers (SBIs) unchanged on Monday after raising the rates for one- and two-week papers by 200 basis points last Friday.

The bank offered one-to-three-day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 10.5, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent on Monday.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 16.13 percent, compared with 15.75 percent on Thursday.
